# HTML Artifact Publisher

A signed-in web app that publishes self-contained HTML pages to private, versioned
links, with a library for accounts and sharing. Agents publish with a CLI. This file
is the agent-facing summary; the full instructions live in the repository.

## Setup

- Human setup page: /agent-setup.html
- Source repository: https://github.com/danmestas/html-artifact-publisher
- Downloadable source bundle (skills, CLI, shared assets — not an installer):
  https://github.com/danmestas/html-artifact-publisher/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
- Read this file from the instance you publish to; do not assume a fixed hostname.
  The install commands below use `$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher`; substitute
  your own dedicated tools directory if you prefer.

## Install the skills

The repository's `skills/` directory holds one folder per skill. Inspect the
instructions and scripts before running them. These commands are safe to run more
than once. They clone only when the destination is absent. They reuse an existing
checkout only when it is a git checkout whose origin is this repository and it still
holds the CLI, `public/` and `skills/publish-html-page`; they never pull or replace
it. An unrelated repository, an empty directory or an incomplete checkout stops with
an error and is left untouched. Each skill is linked into the agent's skill directory
without forcing: existing files, directories and dangling symlinks are skipped and
reported.

```bash
set -e
checkout="$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher"
expected_origin="https://github.com/danmestas/html-artifact-publisher.git"
if [ -e "$checkout" ] || [ -L "$checkout" ]; then
  if [ ! -d "$checkout/.git" ]; then
    echo "Error: $checkout exists but is not a git checkout. Move it aside and rerun; nothing was changed." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  origin="$(git -C "$checkout" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ "$origin" != "$expected_origin" ]; then
    echo "Error: $checkout is a git checkout of ${origin:-<no origin>}, not $expected_origin. Move it aside and rerun; nothing was changed." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  for required in scripts/publish-html.mjs public skills/publish-html-page; do
    if [ ! -e "$checkout/$required" ]; then
      echo "Error: $checkout is missing $required; it is not a usable checkout. Move it aside and rerun; nothing was changed." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  echo "Using existing checkout at $checkout."
else
  git clone "$expected_origin" "$checkout"
fi
mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude/skills"
for skill in publish-html-page artifact-design artifact-runtime artifact-diagrams artifact-dataviz pikchr; do
  target="$HOME/.claude/skills/$skill"
  if [ -e "$target" ] || [ -L "$target" ]; then
    echo "Skipped $skill: $target already exists; left unchanged."
    continue
  fi
  ln -s "$checkout/skills/$skill" "$target"
  echo "Linked $skill -> $checkout/skills/$skill"
done
```

`~/.claude/skills` is Claude Code's user skills directory; other agents use their
equivalent. Add `self-host-publisher` only when setting up a new instance.

Installed skills run from the checkout, not from the skill folder. Resolve it with a
validated suffix, not a bare `readlink` guess: a symlinked skill resolves to
`<checkout>/skills/publish-html-page`, and the result counts only when the CLI,
`public/` and the skill are actually there. A copied skill contains neither, so
nothing is inferred from its location — the retained checkout must be given
explicitly. If neither yields a valid checkout, stop and ask instead of guessing.

```bash
set -e
install_dir="$HOME/.claude/skills/publish-html-page"
resolved="$(readlink -f "$install_dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
candidate=""
case "$resolved" in
  */skills/publish-html-page) candidate="${resolved%/skills/publish-html-page}" ;;
esac
valid_checkout() {
  [ -n "$1" ] && [ -f "$1/scripts/publish-html.mjs" ] && [ -d "$1/public" ] && [ -d "$1/skills/publish-html-page" ]
}
CHECKOUT=""
if valid_checkout "$candidate"; then CHECKOUT="$candidate"; fi
if [ -z "$CHECKOUT" ] && valid_checkout "${HTML_PUBLISHER_CHECKOUT:-}"; then CHECKOUT="$HTML_PUBLISHER_CHECKOUT"; fi
if [ -z "$CHECKOUT" ]; then
  echo "Cannot determine the html-artifact-publisher checkout." >&2
  echo "Install the skill as a symlink to the retained checkout, or set HTML_PUBLISHER_CHECKOUT to it." >&2
  echo "A copied skill does not contain scripts/ or public/ and cannot infer the checkout." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "$CHECKOUT"
```

Then invoke the CLI by absolute path, or change into the checkout first, and pass
absolute artifact paths. Keeping the checkout is necessary but not sufficient: the
command has to name it.

| Skill | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `skills/publish-html-page` | Required. Publish and update pages, link handling. |
| `skills/artifact-design` | Page contract: themes, no network, layout, phones. |
| `skills/artifact-runtime` | `window.artifact`: saved data, self-editing pages, history. |
| `skills/artifact-diagrams` | When a diagram helps, and what it should show. |
| `skills/artifact-dataviz` | Charts, palette, contrast checks. |
| `skills/pikchr` | Draw diagrams in Pikchr; `render.mjs`. |
| `skills/self-host-publisher` | Optional: run a separate copy on another Cloudflare account. |

Node.js 22 or newer (CI uses 24) is enough to publish. Go, TinyGo, Wrangler and a server
deployment are not needed for CLI publishing.

## Environment

`publish` and `list` read two variables:

```bash
export HTML_PUBLISHER_URL="https://this-instance.example"
export HTML_PUBLISHER_TOKEN="replace-with-your-personal-credential"
```

Replace the URL with this instance's origin and the token with the credential you
created. Create a personal credential on /?view=credentials. Load the token from an
environment variable or secret manager. Never put it in a URL, a page, localStorage,
a log, or your output, and never print an edit link, clone URL or token where others
can see it.

## Create versus update

Run the CLI by absolute path from the checkout (`$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher`
below). Pass absolute paths for input files; the CLI resolves its own assets relative
to that checkout, not to the current directory.

```bash
node "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher/scripts/publish-html.mjs" /absolute/path/page.html --title "Report"
node "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher/scripts/publish-html.mjs" update "$EDIT_URL" /absolute/path/page.html --message "Revise report"
node "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher/scripts/publish-html.mjs" read "$READ_OR_EDIT_URL" --out "$OUT_DIR"
node "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher/scripts/publish-html.mjs" history "$URL"
node "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher/scripts/publish-html.mjs" list
node "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher/scripts/publish-html.mjs" delete "$EDIT_URL"
```

Set `EDIT_URL` to the edit link, `READ_OR_EDIT_URL` to a read or edit link, `URL` to
the artifact link, and `OUT_DIR` to a directory path before running these; quoting
keeps tokens and spaces intact. `--out` is optional: without it `read` prints the
page's HTML to stdout instead of writing files.

Alternatively `cd "$HOME/tools/html-artifact-publisher"` and use
`node scripts/publish-html.mjs …` with absolute artifact paths.

Publish once, then `update` that same artifact. Do not publish a new artifact for every
revision. `update` exits 3 if someone published after you read the tip: nothing was
saved; `read` the newer version and build on it. An update whose files already match the
tip exits 1 with "nothing changed". Use the URL and history the instance returns; do not
construct links by hand.

The default TTL is 7d (7 days); `--ttl never` keeps the artifact until it is deleted.

## Links

- Read link `…/v/<id>#<readToken>`: the shareable link. Post it after every publish and
  update. It can read and comment.
- Comment link `…/v/<id>#<commentToken>`: read and comment, not edit.
- Edit link `…/v/<id>#<writeToken>`: update and delete. Keep it private.
- Clone URL `https://editor:<writeToken>@<host>/r/<id>`: for Fossil. Keep it private.

A read link cannot update.

## What a published page can do

- The viewer sandbox blocks external network requests. Pages must be self-contained:
  inline CSS and scripts, and reference attachments by relative paths in the same
  published directory. Small text files travel with the page; images, video, fonts, and
  files over 256 KB are stored separately and uploaded automatically (up to 100 MB each).
- Pages follow light and dark appearance. Ship complete light and dark palettes and do
  not pin a theme in the root element.
- When the viewer injects `window.artifact`, a page can read its files and history, save
  new versions (`publish`), and keep small shared values (`data.get/set/list`). Saving
  requires the edit link. See `skills/artifact-runtime`.
- Each publish or update is a check-in, so history and rollback are available with
  `read`, `history`, and Fossil itself.

## Self-hosting

`skills/self-host-publisher` covers running your own copy on a Cloudflare account; its
full procedure is `docs/self-hosting.md` in the repository. This is separate from using
an existing instance with the CLI.
